title: Emergent algorithm
summary:
An emergent algorithm is an algorithm that exhibits emergent behavior. In essence, an emergent algorithm implements a set of simple building block behaviors that when combined exhibit more complex behaviors. It achieves predictable global effects, does not require global visibility, does not assume any kind of centralized control, and is self-stabilizing.

Examples of emergent algorithms include fuzzy motion controllers for robot movement and cellular automata. Emergent algorithms achieve predictable global effects through self-organization without global knowledge or control. They are used in applications like neural networks and swarm intelligence systems.

The broader concept of emergent computing encompasses models and algorithms with characteristics such as self-organization, aggregative behavior, and cooperative behavior. Representative examples include artificial neural networks, swarm intelligence, membrane systems, and quantum computing. Related topics include evolutionary computation, genetic algorithms, and heuristics.
